## b27ef5e054f4

**Reproduced missing semantic control / suspected shortcut.** At generator
SHA-256
`9a6e13f9fcbaeb0bef6ecbfdb4ecf9bd41b89ec4720ad38afe708450d41c3126`,
288 samples (seeds 0–15, sample indices 0–5, all three difficulty bands)
contained **zero** columns with two or more red cells. The implementation
samples distinct columns, although the rule processes reds bottom-up and uses
previously landed reds as blockers.

A self-check-valid counterexample (`dc123f2cbc542623`) places reds at `(0,2)`,
`(2,2)`, and `(0,4)` with a blocker at `(6,2)`. The authoritative rule lands
the same-column reds at `(4,2)` and `(5,2)`, proving red-on-red stacking is part
of the executable semantics. A learner trained only on current outputs can use
the weaker independent-per-column “fall to static blocker/border” rule and never
learn collision ordering. Add a scheduled same-column stack profile and a rival
that ignores landed reds.

triage.reason: Brief-reviewed under October 3 lightweight policy; preserve reported evidence and findings. Shared-tool requests consolidated separately. No maintainer battery/test/private-solve rerun or automatic training admission.
